lead: the rate you named in a doorway when you were twenty-six is still the rate for those eleven people, and your working week is built out of afternoons you agreed to before you had the tools.
sun: what your hands do for a living, other people arrange by contract and renegotiate every few years. you arranged it by answering. an answer given standing in somebody's doorway lands as terms, and every job you took on became a standing arrangement inside its first ten minutes, priced at what seemed fair that morning. none has come up for review in the decades since.
moon: the answering is faster than the assessing and always has been. you are down the stairs and in the van before the size of the thing has been established, and the yes is out of you while the person is still describing it. everywhere else that would cost a wasted evening. here it fixes the next thirty years, because what your sun does with a yes is keep it.
pull: you price a job in the first minute and honour the price for thirty years. the arriving is instinct, the keeping is character, and neither has ever asked what the work is worth.
tension: people call you reliable and mean the picking up, not the twenty years attached to it. your diary has no room in it and no mechanism for making room: a client from your first year holds the same standing as the work you would rather be doing, and no conversation exists that would end one. the newest jobs go at the edges of the week, in evenings, and the oldest keep the good hours.
cost: somebody who called you once at a bad hour has had first claim on your working life ever since, at a price set before you knew the trade. the money is the visible part. the whole shape of what you do was decided by who happened to reach you early, and the people you would have chosen came along after the week was full.

lead: two teenagers in a shared room agreed something out loud, in about nine words, and the family you came from has been organised around those nine words for thirty-four years without anyone else being told.
sun: children agree things all the time and the agreements evaporate. yours took. it was entered on purpose, between equals, with nothing at all enforcing it, and it has outlasted the house it was made in, both of your parents, and every adult arrangement either of you has entered since. the wording has never been revisited, because a thing entered that way holds without attention.
moon: what you undertook, you carry, and carrying leaves nothing on the surface. the calls at odd hours, the money that went, the years you held his worst stretch inside you and let none of it reach the rest of them — from outside that is a quiet man with a close brother. none of it has ever looked like effort from where the rest of them sit.
pull: the family you came from runs on a sentence two boys said to each other, and the ones it protects were never told a sentence exists.
tension: laughing, at a table with everyone there, he said he has no memory of that night, and that is not something you can raise. an agreement kept by one side is still an agreement, and this one holds the whole shape of your family — the visits, the money, which of you takes the calls — on the memory of a single person, with nothing anywhere to show it was ever made.
cost: a person can be held for decades without once being asked to acknowledge that he is being held, and you have done it so completely that he has been free the whole time. storage is what it turns into. what began as two children looking after each other is now a fifty-year-old man's affairs kept in a place he cannot see, by somebody who cannot put them down.

lead: everything binding in your life has your single name on it, and everything that ever felt like rest had six people in it and no names at all. The Crown only ever addresses a single name.
sun: an undertaking has to be addressed to somebody. it names one party, it is answerable by one party, and when you gave your word twenty years ago the word came out of a single mouth belonging to a single person with a single set of obligations. your daytime life runs in that register, named and individual and on the hook, and you fit it worst of anything you do.
moon: a line drawn from your sun to your moon goes through the centre of the wheel, and your moon is where it comes out the other side. what is standing there is a crowd: the version of you that is one of several, uncounted, indistinguishable at any distance, and that is the only condition in which you have ever relaxed. it is unavailable to a named party.
pull: the promise names you, and holds. the good years were the ones where nobody outside could tell which of you had done what, and nobody inside was keeping track.
tension: the work you promised into was five people and a shared thing, and it is a hard fact of groups that they thin. two moved, one stopped speaking, and what is left is you and the person you actually gave your word to, running an arrangement whose whole point was the number. you are held to it exactly. pressure took the group apart and left the one part of it that cannot come apart.
cost: the thing still runs, on time, twenty years in, because one person said something once — an obligation does the work five people used to do. what does not survive is the reason you joined. you are the last one still bound and the only one who never wanted to be here alone, and there is no clause about the others leaving.

lead: quarter past six, the same door, the same two bodies, thirty-one years. you are the stronger one and you have spent all of it half a stride back, and no word about it has passed between you.
sun: it started as a sentence said in a bad year: the two of you would go out every morning, and neither would be the one who stopped it. that sentence is now the oldest arrangement in either of your lives. your appetite, your weight, your sleep and what you drink on a weeknight sit underneath it, because the undertaking predates all of them and has outranked them since.
moon: the pace was set by the slower body and you fell in behind it on the first morning, on purpose, and have stayed there by choice ever since. thirty years of that shapes a person: you are strong in a way that has never been tested, fit to somebody else's ceiling, with a top end you have not visited since your twenties. no morning since has been an open question.
pull: the body you have is the body of an agreement — kept every morning for thirty years, at somebody else's pace, by somebody who could have gone faster on any of them.
tension: his knees went two winters ago and the distance has come down by half, and none of that has touched the hour or the door. no sentence that would end it has ever formed in you. the morning it stops will be a morning somebody could not come, and until then you go on covering a distance that does nothing for you, in shoes you replace every year.
cost: thirty-one years without a missed morning is a rarer thing than any race you could have entered, and none of it ran on wanting to go. that is also where the ceiling came from. the pace, the distance and the appetite were all fixed by an agreement made in a bad year, and your body has been the property of that year ever since.
